page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server designed for compute-intensive and machine learning workloads. The system features 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 375.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.72 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the server bundles two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 62892.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 64768.69, both placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached reads reaching 4985.78 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 211.9 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is in the top 10% tier at 15.2 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression reaches 430.84 GB/sec. In database and web operations, the instance processed 70.17 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved a static web serving throughput of 60.34 GB/sec.

The dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs excel in artificial intelligence workloads, particularly LLM inference. For a medium 7B parameter model, the server achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds of 6275.36 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 141.42 tokens per second. These metrics make the instance highly suitable for large language model deployment, deep learning training, high-performance computing, and complex data science pipelines. The combination of high-capacity system memory, fast NVMe storage, and dual enterprise GPUs offers a balanced resource density for demanding parallel processing tasks.
